**Conformal prediction turns held-out errors into a prediction set with a stated coverage target.** Train the model on one subset, then measure how poorly it fits each example in a separate calibration subset. These nonconformity scores establish a threshold for accepting candidate outcomes. [1](https://arxiv.org/abs/2107.07511)

For regression, a simple score is absolute residual. If the calibrated threshold is 3, a prediction of 20 yields interval [17,23]. The interval's width reflects the calibration errors under this simple method, not a claim of constant conditional uncertainty everywhere.

**The finite-sample rank correction matters.** With n calibration scores, use rank $\lceil(n+1)(1-\alpha)\rceil$, with the appropriate infinite threshold if that rank exceeds n. Under exchangeability, the new score's rank among all n+1 scores gives the marginal coverage argument.

“90% coverage” means at least the target fraction over repeated examples under the assumptions, not 90% correctness for this particular case or every subgroup. Sets can be too wide to be useful. Evaluate coverage and size together, and avoid repeatedly tuning on the same calibration set. Distribution shift can break exchangeability and the associated guarantee.

**Technical details and references.**

Split data into model-training and calibration sets. Fit the model without calibration labels, compute calibration nonconformity scores, and take the order statistic at rank $\lceil(n+1)(1-\alpha)\rceil$, with the appropriate infinite-threshold convention if rank exceeds $n$. [1](https://arxiv.org/abs/2107.07511)

$$C(x)=\{y:s(x,y)\le\hat q\}.$$

Exchangeability makes the new example's score rank uniform, giving marginal coverage at least $1-\alpha$ with conservative tie handling. No parametric outcome distribution is required, but exchangeability is a substantive assumption. Coverage is not conditional correctness for each individual or subgroup, and sets can be unhelpfully large. Evaluate size/coverage by relevant slices and reassess under deployment shift; using calibration data to tune repeatedly can break the guarantee.
